analysis.title: A Quantum of Solace
key_insights: US equities stayed under pressure over the past week despite upbeat Nvidia earnings and strong demand for the Anthropic IPO. Drags cited are Nvidia governance scandals and concern about AI regulation under a Democratic Congress.

The October FOMC minutes held few surprises and affirmed market expectations for a rate hike in December. The author expects 25bps and sees a 50bps move as unwarranted unless the next CPI release surprises materially to the upside.

The author argues policy is not far behind the curve. Policy rates are slightly above the Fed's long-term neutral estimate, and the inflation overshoot is more modest than in 2022 (inflation peaked at 8%, rates started from 0%). Only incremental tightening is seen as needed.

A further Fed hike is expected in Q1 2027, with the Fed very data dependent. Inflation is expected to peak in a few months. The FOMC may stop tightening after next spring if inflation is set to trend lower.
The author expects the Fed to tolerate CPI gains in the high 2s against a somewhat restrictive policy stance. Strong growth from business investment may keep inflation sticky on the way down.

AI-related debt issuance is slated at about $650bn in 2026. Market expectations embed about $1 trillion for next year. The author suggests taking the 'under' on that figure because Democratic regulation may cause capital-raising plans to peak.

Corporate and government bond issuance over the past year has added to term and credit premia globally. Continued near-exponential growth in AI debt supply would add pressure because the supply of capital is struggling to keep pace with demand.

The front end of the US yield curve is seen as slightly cheap relative to fair value. The author recommends a modest overweight in US duration and sees yields in Europe and Japan as somewhat attractive.

Eurozone inflation is expected to peak higher than in the US but to fall faster through 2027 because of the weaker Eurozone economy. UK inflation is expected to peak near 5%, likely in the April print.

The Bank of England may deliver fewer hikes than are discounted because of the dovish instincts of the MPC, and UK data show limited pass-through from energy prices. Rate cuts could return to the agenda by end-2027 if inflation recedes.

Japan's Q3 GDP contracted on the quarter, partly from one-off factors such as a record 37 days of rain. Underlying growth is seen near 1% and inflation near 2.5%. The author expects the BoJ to continue normalisation in December, and sees a delay under pressure from PM Takaichi as ill-advised because it could renew yen weakness.

Credit spreads softened in the past week with equity weakness, and heavy hyperscaler issuance affects relative value across credit. The author thinks much of the bad news on supply is already in spreads, and European spreads have scope to retrace recent widening if supply stops being revised higher.
The Middle East low-level conflict has no end in sight, but reports that the crude oil market is moving back into surplus as shipping continues are keeping a lid on energy prices.

With energy prices well below last month's peaks, the author says headline US CPI could be as low as -0.3% in the December release. Core is more important for the Fed, but headline optics may improve before the next FOMC.

tension_points.bear_case: Market talk of a 50bps move reflects a view that the Fed is behind the curve and needs a larger move.
